newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AMNESTY FOR MAN WHO HELPED S. AFRICAN EDITOR FLEE.
newsitem.headline: AMNESTY FOR MAN WHO HELPED S. AFRICAN EDITOR FLEE.

text.p: The man who helped former newspaper editor Donald Woods to flee persecution by apartheid police for his friendship with black activist Steve Biko was granted amnesty on Tuesday by South Africa's truth commission.

Donald Card, 68, was given amnesty by the post-apartheid Truth and Reconciliation Commission for breaking past laws by helping Woods to violate his banning order and to escape across the borders of South Africa.
The commission said in a statement that as gross violations of human rights were not at issue, no public hearing was held to decide Card's request for amnesty.
Card was a former mayor of East London, the Eastern Cape city where Woods befriended Biko, and a member of the now- defunct Progressive Federal Party (PFP).
Biko and Woods were immortalised in the film "Cry Freedom", based on the biography Woods wrote after he went into exile in Britain to escape police harassment because of his friendship with Biko.

The black consciousness leader died of brain damage in September 1977. He was the most prominent black activist to die while detained without trial under draconian security laws used to suppress opposition to apartheid.
Five former security policemen said in January they were ready to come clean on the severe beatings meted out to Biko. Their amnesty applications have not been completed.
